integrity: The accessible 2010 same-object publisher preview was inspected for the exact equations, fixed-point and bifurcation scope, and physical interpretation. A complete open 2013 same-object article was inspected through its model definition, hyperchaotic parameters, equilibria, control construction, synchronization results, and references; targeted full-text searches found no conditional-expectation, invariant-measure, or variance theorem matching the accepted statement. Published 2010 and 2019 boundedness work was compared for quadratic Lyapunov cancellation and invariant-region coverage, and no novelty is claimed for those prior techniques. A mathematical treatment of generalized Lorenz equations was checked for primary MSC 37L30. The heightwise conditional law, the two stationary moment identities, the mean-height interval, and the speed-defect formula were independently reconstructed, and the algebra was replayed with the packaged checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is conditional on compactly supported invariant probability measures and does not establish chaotic or hyperchaotic attractor existence for arbitrary parameters.
The heightwise law determines only the conditional mean of \(xy\) given \(z\), not the full conditional distribution.
The interval \(0<m<r\) is a necessary stationary condition for non-origin states, not a complete existence classification.
The historically earlier 1996 and 2010 sources were not assigned invented day-level publication dates; the structured date uses the earliest checked day-resolved same-object source.
Some early same-object material was available only as publisher previews or bibliographic records.
A differently phrased equivalent invariant-measure identity could remain in unindexed literature.
title: Heightwise wave-feedback calibration and stationary moment geometry in the Lorenz–Stenflo flow
